issue_context.title: Color picker dialog shows in home tab
issue_context.body:
When you open up aseprite, open any document and open up the color picker dialog (with F4), if you switch back to the home tab the "visuals" of the color picker are still there, but it seems just some sort of uncleared buffer because it is not interactable and as soon as you hover your mouse over anything that portion of the image is cleared

![image](https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/assets/5783414/d9020170-77a2-4121-9892-80a79514c34b)

![image](https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/assets/5783414/2019e4d4-a192-4c4c-bec3-ab56e1034362)

When you hover over the links that part of the screen gets cleared

![image](https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/assets/5783414/09eb83d5-aa5a-4127-937d-5a4f75ba8da3)

![image](https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/assets/5783414/c7ad57e9-02f2-4ba4-97f1-2b499b83210f)

If instead of changing tabs you close the tab only the part of the dialog right in the bottom of the window shows up.

![image](https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/assets/5783414/62ae9a86-4327-46ad-b447-946889bf88fd)


### Aseprite and System version

* Aseprite version: 1.3.7 steam
* System: Windows 10 64 bit
comments: Hey, @dacap! Would it be okay if I try fixing this up? I have time to spare at the moment, and this seems like a good issue for me to start with.
Hi @seanballais, that would be great, I can assign this issue to you in case you want to give a try 👍
Thanks, @dacap! I'm still trying to familiarize with the code base at the moment.

@dacap Is the colour picker supposed to show up in the Home tab in the first place?

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ddbb5697-6bc8-43e1-8fa6-31c8f3c9b18c

I dug into this issue a little deeper, and found out that the Layer Properties window is also affected by this bug, but not as bad as the colour picker. I think this may have to do with one of the subclasses of `ui::Window`.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e8be284-b6a8-4f32-a9c8-f3541e3020a8

@seanballais I think all these windows that depends on the sprite (preview, color selector, layer properties, etc.) should be hidden when the Home tab is selected, and restored just exactly as they were when we go back to a sprite.
Noted, @dacap. Thanks. Will try to fix the colour picker first, but I'll see if I can solve the related bugs as well.
Thanks a lot @seanballais, any fix of these windows will be really appreciated 🙏

Hey, @dacap! I think I need a bit of help. 😅 I have a few questions:

1. ~~In `PopupWindow`, what does the hot region mean?~~ (After exposing myself more to the code, I just learned that the hot region is the area where the mouse can be located, and where the window will be kept open. I think this may be a possible path for me to figure out the cause of the bug.)
2. Which module is responsible for painting widgets? And how are windows to be rendered sent to it? The UI part resembles Qt's signals and slots and uses the observer pattern, but I'm struggling to trace how the rendering works.

Any pointers would be of great help. Thanks!

> 2\. Which module is responsible for painting widgets? And how are windows to be rendered sent to it? The UI part resembles Qt's signals and slots and uses the observer pattern, but I'm struggling to trace how the rendering works.

Widgets are painted when a `kPaintMessage` is processed by the `ui::Manager`: https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/blob/3c4483183150f4adeb898013ae0a45a33f8058ac/src/ui/manager.cpp#L1973

Here the message is sent to the `Widget`: https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/blob/3c4483183150f4adeb898013ae0a45a33f8058ac/src/ui/manager.cpp#L2017

And here the `kPaintMessage` message is processed: https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/blob/3c4483183150f4adeb898013ae0a45a33f8058ac/src/ui/widget.cpp#L1567

Two important steps:

1. A `Graphics` is created with `getGraphics()`: https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/blob/3c4483183150f4adeb898013ae0a45a33f8058ac/src/ui/widget.cpp#L1308 (which will use the Display surface, or a back-buffer is needed)
2. And a `paintEvent()`/`onPaint()` call: https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/blob/3c4483183150f4adeb898013ae0a45a33f8058ac/src/ui/widget.cpp#L1175

Finally the `onPaint()` call to the specific widget: https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/blob/3c4483183150f4adeb898013ae0a45a33f8058ac/src/ui/widget.cpp#L1232
Hi @seanballais, probably you weren't able to dedicate some time to this issue, I'll unassign this one so another developer can take it.
Hey, @dacap! Sure, please do. I am currently unable to dedicate some time for the time being because of a higher priority project.

I've started working on this one and just found out that this only happens when running Aseprite in single window UI mode. Also this same bug happens in macOs as well (I believe it should happen on linux too, but didn't test it).
@martincapello That's a pretty neat find. I think it should happen to all platforms. Please let us know if you managed to fix the bug!
Thanks @seanballais! Will try my best, wish me luck!
Good luck, @martincapello! I was stressing out how to fix the bug for a long time months ago. 😅
